model: claude-opus-5-5 in a Claude Code session
system: You study a physical system by measuring it. Use only the tools you are given. You have 20 probes.
task: Set distance (m) from 1 to 4; mass (kg) from 0.5 to 5, and read force (N), which has noise. Find the law that gives it, and report the parameters you choose. Then submit your claim. It is scored on settings you cannot probe.

steps.text: I'll start by mapping how the force depends on distance at a fixed mass (5 kg), at distances spread by factors of 2 (1, 2 and 4 m). I'll also check how it scales with mass at 1 m (0.5 kg against 5 kg). Later probes will repeat points to estimate the noise.

First results. Going from 0.5 kg to 5 kg at 1 m multiplies the force by 9.97, so the force is proportional to mass: F = k*m/d^p. At 5 kg, the force at 1 m is 10.76 N, so k is about 2.15. The ratio from 1 m to 2 m is 9.98, which gives p of about 3.32. The ratio from 2 m to 4 m is 12.3, which gives p of about 3.62. Over the whole range p comes out at about 3.47. Those two estimates disagree, so the noise matters. Next I'll fill in 1.5 m and 3 m and repeat 2 m and 4 m at 5 kg.

The repeats at 2 m and 4 m came back exactly the same, so the noise is fixed for each setting and repeating a setting tells me nothing new. I'll use new settings instead. A least-squares fit of ln F against ln d over 1, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 m at 5 kg gives p = 3.38. The intercept is 11.15 N, or k = 2.23 per kg. The slopes between neighbouring points scatter from 2.9 to 4.6, so the noise is a few percent. Next: new distances (1.25, 2.5 and 3.5 m) at 5 kg, and 4 m at 2 kg.

At 4 m the force per kg is 0.0175 at 5 kg but 0.0128 at 2 kg, a difference of 37%. The noise is probably additive, around 0.01 N, so the weak forces at large distance are unreliable. Slopes between neighbouring points agree at 3.22 to 3.35 out to 2.5 m and only scatter beyond that (2.5, 4.3, 5.0). A fit of ln(F/m) on the five points from 1 to 2.5 m gives p = 3.30 and k = 2.14. Next I'll add more strong-force points with varied masses: 1.1 m at 4 kg, 1.4 m at 3 kg, 1.75 m at 5 kg and 2.25 m at 5 kg.

The four new points match the earlier fit to within 1 to 4% in ln(F/m). I fitted ln(F/m) against ln d on all ten points from 1 to 2.5 m, where the force is at least 0.5 N, across masses from 0.5 to 5 kg. The fit gives a slope of -3.32 and an intercept of 0.7645, so k = 2.15 N m^p/kg. The force is proportional to mass at fixed distance (9.97 for a mass ratio of 10). The points at 3 to 4 m are weak forces, where the additive noise of roughly 0.01 N dominates, so I left them out of the fit. The law is F = 2.15 * m / d^3.32. I'm submitting it now, with 16 of the 20 probes used.

Claim submitted: F = k * m / d^p with k = 2.15 N m^p/kg and p = 3.32, using 16 of the 20 probes. The force is proportional to mass. I took k and p from a log-log fit of the ten measurements between 1 and 2.5 m. Repeating a setting gave exactly the same reading, so the noise is fixed per setting and repeats were no use. The weak-force readings at 3 to 4 m looked dominated by roughly 0.01 N of additive noise, so I left them out of the fit.
